newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-49ERS' YOUNG TO START SUNDAY AGAINST WASHINGTON.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-49ERS' YOUNG TO START SUNDAY AGAINST WASHINGTON.

text.p: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Steve Young, who has suffered two concussions in the last four weeks, will start Sunday's road game against the Washington Redskins, coach George Seifert announced Wednesday.
Young was told in a Tuesday meeting with Seifert that he would be the starter.
"We made our decision based on science, and the way everyone feels about it, the way I feel about it, and the way the team feels about it," Young said.

"I feel I'm well educated and that I've been given enough information where I can make a rational decision, and know the risks. I don't think I take any more risk this week than any other guy from my team."

Young, who has also been hampered by a groin injury, did not play in Sunday's 38-20 home victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Elvis Grbac started against Baltimore after replacing Young the previous week in a 20-17 overtime loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Against Dallas, Young started but suffered his second concussion when he was hit by lineman Chad Hennings and linebacker Jim Schwantz in the second quarter. He played another series, but was replaced by Grbac and did not return.

Young suffered his first concussion on October 27 at Houston when he was clobbered by Oilers linebacker Michael Barrow on San Francisco's first series. Third-stringer Jeff Brohm replaced Young and guided the Niners to a 10-9 victory.
"I've taken a lot of hits over my career," Young said. "I hope that we've had two unique ones, and that like lightning hopefully doesn't strike three times."
Young said his groin injury, which forced him to miss three games earlier this season, is about 95 percent healed.

The 49ers and Redskins are tied with the Green Bay Packers for the best record in the NFC at 8-3. The winner of Sunday's game would take a step towards clinching the conference's best mark and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs.
"Steve's our starter and he feels like he's ready to go," said Seifert. "The doctors have turned him loose, so he's going. He feels he's as healthy as he's felt and ready to go."
Young, the NFL Player of the Year in 1994 and Super Bowl 29 Most Valuable Player, has completed 96-of-154 passes for 1,119 yards, five touchdowns and four interceptions this season.
The 35-year-old Young did not miss a game from 1992 to 1994, passing for more than 11,000 yards and 89 touchdowns, but missed five games last season.
